If we plug in $x=0$ we get the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ so  we apply L'Hopital's rule to find the limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+5x)-5x}{{x}^{2}} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{[\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+5x)-5x]}^{′}}{[{x}^{2}]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(\frac{5}{1+5x}-5)}{2x} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(\frac{1}{1+5x}-1)}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+5x)-5x}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{5}{2}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(\frac{1}{1+5x}-1)}{x} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{[(1+5x)^{-1}-1]}^{′}}{[x]^{′}} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{lim}_{x\to 0}(-5(1+5x)^{-2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}(-5) \\  & =-\frac{25}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
